en: Udāna 1.6 Mahākassapasutta Thus have I heard:
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now at that time, the Venerable Mahākassapa was dwelling in the Pippali Cave, afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.
Then, after some time, the Venerable Mahākassapa recovered from that illness.
Then, when the Venerable Mahākassapa had recovered from that illness, it occurred to him:
"What if I were to enter Rājagaha for alms?
At that time, about five hundred deities were making an effort to provide almsfood for the Venerable Mahākassapa.
Then the Venerable Mahākassapa, having declined those five hundred deities, dressed in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms, heading toward the streets of the poor,
the streets of the destitute, and the streets of the weavers.
The Blessed One saw the Venerable Mahākassapa walking for alms in Rājagaha, heading toward the streets of the poor, the streets of the destitute, and the streets of the weavers.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
who is independent, tamed, and established in the essence;”
"One whose taints are destroyed and who has vomited out faults— him I call a brahmin.
